items.headline: Nvidia's chief executive resigns effective immediately; the CFO steps in as interim CEO
items.why: The stock sits roughly a third below its October peak and the company reports quarterly results on Nov 17, so the first read on guidance under interim leadership is now the key event for the whole AI-chip trade.

sources.title: Nvidia Stock Falls Below $165 After Its CEO Resigns

items.headline: Chip stocks extend selloff on Friday: AMD down about 9%, Broadcom down more than 5%, Nvidia's losing streak reaches six weeks
items.why: Weakness spread beyond one name, which signals investors are repricing the whole AI-hardware group rather than reacting to a single headline.

sources.title: Wall Street Slides As Chip Stocks Extend Selloff

items.headline: OpenAI reportedly tells lawmakers it backs tighter limits on China's access to AI chips and chipmaking equipment
items.why: Lawmakers want to attach three export-control bills to the annual defense bill; if they pass, they would add compliance cost for chipmakers and could strain the US-China trade truce.

sources.title: OpenAI Reportedly Backs Tighter AI Chip Controls on China

items.headline: Bitcoin drops to about $62,080, its lowest since July, then rebounds above $65,000; down nearly 15% on the week
items.why: A break to four-month lows with sentiment at extreme fear shows sellers still control the tape; the $62K area is now the level to watch.

sources.title: Bitcoin Falls to Four-Month Low Near $62K as Crypto Market Slides

items.headline: US spot bitcoin ETFs lose $2.35B over two weeks; the largest fund posts 11 straight sessions of outflows
items.why: Sustained ETF selling removes the main institutional bid that supported prices this year.

sources.title: Bitcoin: $2.35 billion leaves BlackRock's ETF in 11 sessions

items.headline: Ether falls 19.5% in a week to about $1,834; Fear & Greed index hits 10 and total crypto market cap slips to $2.26 trillion
items.why: Ether is falling faster than bitcoin, which is the usual pattern when leverage is being cleared across the broader market.

sources.title: Bitcoin Falls to Four-Month Low Near $62K as Crypto Market Slides

items.headline: October CPI rises 0.4% against 0.3% expected; core CPI +0.3% for a third straight month; markets price a December Fed hike at about 85%
items.why: Inflation is re-accelerating while the Fed is leaning toward hiking rather than cutting, which pressures long-duration assets and the gold price.

sources.title: Inflation remained elevated in October, CPI report shows, upping odds of Fed interest rate hike - CBS News

items.headline: October producer prices up 6.5% year on year, the largest annual rise since November 2022; core PPI up 4.9%
items.why: Pipeline inflation this high makes it harder for the Fed to pause; the monthly gain was slightly below forecast, which is why a 25bp move is favored over 50bp.

sources.title: Gold prices testing resistance at $3,900 as producers prices continue to rise - Kitco

items.headline: Iran ceasefire hopes fade after the US president says no deal is needed; a gas tanker reportedly hit a mine in the Strait of Hormuz
items.why: Hormuz shipping risk keeps an energy-supply premium in oil even as the IEA reports a surplus, and it keeps inflation expectations elevated.

items.headline: Gold hits a 13-month low of $3,852 on Thursday and ends near $3,884, down about 5% on the week
items.why: Rate-hike expectations, higher yields and a stronger dollar are overpowering gold's safe-haven role; $3,900 is now resistance, and most Wall Street analysts surveyed expect further declines.

sources.title: Wall Street bears abound after inflation sours Fed outlook, gold drops below $3,900/oz - Kitco

items.headline: Brent settles at $95.84 and WTI at $88.56, each down about 2.5% on the week after the prior week's drop of 13-17%
items.why: Oil has fallen two straight weeks from a six-month high, but supply risk around Hormuz is keeping it near $96 Brent.

items.headline: IEA says the oil market moved into surplus for the first time since the Iran war began, and cuts its 2026 demand outlook to a 2.7 million bpd contraction
items.why: Rising supply and shrinking demand are a bearish counterweight to geopolitical risk, though the agency still flags diesel tightness into 2027.

items.headline: S&P 500 closes at 7,560.87 (+2.5% on the week), ending a four-week losing streak; Nasdaq Composite closes at 25,135.96 (+2.3%)
items.why: The weekly bounce held even with a Friday chip-led drop, but it is a rebound inside a downtrend until the index reclaims its prior highs.

items.why: A failed reclaim of $3,900 keeps the structure bearish; analysts surveyed cite downside targets well below the current price.
